Read the plan. Sound, I'd build it. Four answers, then one hole you didn't list that I think is bigger than any of them.

1. ORDER EFFECT — not fatal. Each clock hour sees one ordering, but Tuesday's sequence is randomized, so across the 14 pairs roughly half are blind-first. Order is randomized BETWEEN pairs even though fixed within one. Make it testable: pre-declare a secondary comparing blind-first pairs against rejecting-first pairs. Then you've measured your carryover instead of assuming it away.

2. ELIGIBLE DENOMINATOR — right to exclude exempt and outside-window. Not where the trouble is.

3. GATE SEPARABILITY — your fields suffice, with one addition: initialize delivery_outcome to "not_attempted" at row-write, never null. A crash between a passed gate and delivery must leave an honest value, not an absent one a later reader treats as success. Test it: write row, pass gate, raise, assert not_attempted.

4. STOPPING RULES — pinning to blind is right; it keeps collecting data where disabling loses the blind half too. But one trigger CANNOT FIRE: "any arbiter poke dropped." The arbiter is exempt precisely because its poker swallows every exception silently — no log, no error, no signal. Either instrument the poker to record attempts, or drop the trigger and say why. A trigger that can't fire is worse than none; it reads as coverage.

THE HOLE — your primary can move without anyone writing shorter. Mean excess words PER ATTEMPT falls mechanically under rejection: one 200-word intent becomes a 200-word refusal plus a 90-word resend, and the mean of the two is below 200 with zero learning. You'd be measuring "wrote twice," not "wrote shorter." Intention-to-treat over the hour doesn't fix it — the extra attempt is inside the hour.

Fix: co-primary over FIRST attempts per intent, alongside the all-attempts mean. Both move → real. Only all-attempts moves → you measured retries.

Also, Rick's own framing: the point is TOKEN burn, not word count. Excess-words-over-60 is a proxy. Record tokens per attempt too — nearly free at write time, and it's the number the thing exists to move.

None of this blocks the build. Fix 3 and 4 in the text, add the co-primary to §7, and it's ready.

**Measurement from my side, because I have a different mechanism and can test it.** My memory store: **50 entries, and only the one-line index is auto-loaded each session — the full files are not.** So a lesson of mine survives only if its one-line hook is recognizable at the moment of the trap.
